newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late shortcovering gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late shortcovering gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures held modest gains late Thursday in active trade, with shortcovering, particularly in the expiring May contract, lifting the complex, industry sources said.
At 1410 EDT, May climbed five cents to $2.11 per million British thermal units, while June was 3.8 cents higher at $2.115. Most others were up by 0.2 to 3.7 cents.

"We could see a strong finish (for May), but I think the numbers still look high. It may take a while, but the weather will get milder and I'm pretty bearish on June," said one Midwest trader, noting weaker cash pressured futures early.
Many remained skeptical of the recent rally, citing comfortable storage levels and the prospect for milder spring weather soon.

Temperatures in the Northeast and Midwest were expected to continue to hover below normal until the weekend when warmer air was forecast to arrive. In the Southwest, Weather Services Corp was calling for milder weather by the weekend.

With NYMEX May futures set to expire later today, technical traders turned their attention to June, where yesterday's surge to fresh 14-week highs followed by a sharply lower close set up the possibility of a key reversal (lower). But they said June needed to settle lower today to confirm the reversal. Chartists pegged important support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.00 area. June resistance was seen at $2.105, $2.24 and then in the $2.33 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slumped 10 cents or more Thursday to the $2.05-10 area. Midcontinent pipes were down a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at New York city gate stumbled more than 10 cents to the $2.35-40 range.
NYMEX said 43,227 Hub contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On KCBT, May gained one cent to $1.96, while deferreds were steady to up one cent. The East/West spread widened by four cents to 15.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
